title: The Turing Way
description: 'Welcome to The Turing Way handbook to reproducible, ethical and collaborative data science.' Open, community-written handbook not meant to be read start to finish, with Pathways, five guides (Reproducible Research; Project Design; Communication; Collaboration; Ethical Research) and a Community Handbook. The Guide for Reproducible Research has chapters on Overview (with Definitions), Open Research (including Open Notebooks), Version Control, Licensing, Research Data Management, Reproducible Environments, BinderHub, Code Documentation, Code Quality, Code Testing, Code Reviewing Process, Reusable Code, Continuous Integration, Reproducible Research with Make, Research Compendia, Risk Assessment and Case Studies. The Guide for Project Design covers scoping and planning (a Getting Started Checklist, project management frameworks, project repositories), stakeholders, information management, data security and governance, missing data handling and risks of bias.

limitations: No preregistration chapter: the Guide for Project Design names 'preregistration of research protocols' only in its introduction, and the Getting Started Checklist does not mention preregistration or negative results. Preregistration-style planning comes from cruwell-evans-2021.

No chapter on Jupyter notebooks as such: 'Open Notebooks' concerns open lab-notebook practice; notebook reproducibility falls under Reproducible Environments, BinderHub and Research Compendia, which were seen in the chapter list but not opened.
Negative results and limitations sections are mentioned only in passing; there is no dedicated chapter.
